Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of  KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . items.title: CVE-2026-105769 — kaniko can send the build's Azure (Entra ID) access token to lookalike ACR registry hosts
items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-105769 affectant github.com/chainguard-dev/kaniko (go) (score CVSS 9.3).

kaniko can send the build's Azure (Entra ID) access token to lookalike ACR registry hosts

The flaw is in the Azure Container Registry (ACR) credential helper, github.com/chrismellard/docker-credential-acr-env . kaniko links it into the executor and warmer (the built-in helper) and also builds it as the standalone docker-credential-acr-env binary.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-105769 affectant github.com/chainguard-dev/kaniko (go) (score CVSS 9.3).

kaniko can send the build's Azure (Entra ID) access token to lookalike ACR registry hosts

The flaw is in the Azure Container Registry (ACR) credential helper, github.com/chrismellard/docker-credential-acr-env . kaniko links it into the executor and warmer (the built-in helper) and also builds it as the standalone docker-credential-acr-env binary. The helper decides whether a host is an ACR registry with an unanchored regex, so any hostname that contains .azurecr.io (or .azurecr.cn , .azurecr.de , .azurecr.us ) passes. The upstream module is unmaintained and has no fixed release. The Go vulnerability database tracks the upstream flaw as GO-2026-6225 .

You are affected if you run kaniko before v1.25.20 on Dockerfiles, or build arguments, that you don't fully control, in an environment where the helper can get an Azure identity:

You do not need to use ACR, or configure the helper, to be affected. kaniko consults the built-in helper for any registry that has no credentials in your Docker config and is not a Google or Amazon ECR registry, and every lookalike host falls in that set. That covers base images in FROM lines and images in COPY --from= . kaniko asks for credentials before it contacts the registry, so the attacker's registry doesn't need to request authentication.

If your Docker config.json sets "credsStore": "acr-env" , the standalone binary is consulted for every registry as well. Before v1.25.20 this setting broke pulls from non-ACR registries, so it is uncommon.

The helper puts the token in both the Authorization: Bearer header and the access_token form field of a POST to https:// /oauth2/exchange , so the attacker receives a live access token for Azure

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

DigiCert explained that over the summer, an internal business system was "externally accessible when that was not intended," and someone had created an unauthorized account.

Internet security firm DigiCert reported a data breach involving an internal business system that was left exposed and eventually accessed by someone outside of the company.

The Utah-based company did not respond to requests for comment but posted a lengthy post-mortem on Mozilla's Bugzilla platform explaining the situation.

DigiCert, which is a certificate authority and offers other corporate security services, said the incident began in February 2025 when an internal business system was moved out of a VPN-restricted network, making it accessible externally. Certificates typically help to verify the security of web servers.

“Beginning on 2026-06-21, DigiCert determined that the business system was externally accessible when that was not intended, and that an unassigned account had been created,” the company said, adding that the issue was fixed by July 2.

On October 19, DigiCert confirmed that the database was accessed starting on June 27 and that it was a “reportable event.” The accessed data included customer names, business email addresses, phone numbers as well as documents like driver’s licenses, passports or utility bills and other info.

A spokesperson for the company declined to say whether the attackers have contacted DigiCert, telling Recorded Future News that they are “focused on providing our customers with information relevant to them about the incident.”

Incident de sécurité rapporté par Infosecurity Mag.

SlippyNunchucks used DNS hijacking to turn Sogou brand promotions into a malware channel

A China-aligned group has hijacked the brand-promotion mechanism of Sogou Input Method to deliver the DarkVigil toolset to users in six countries, turning legitimate application traffic into a malware distribution channel.

ESET researcher Anh Ho detailed the activity in research published on November 4, naming the group SlippyNunchucks and tracing its activity to at least September 15, 2023. ESET assessed with high confidence that the group is associated with a nation-state surveillance effort aligned with Chinese government interests.

The campaign began on July 1, 2026, when users of Sogou Input Method, a popular Chinese-language keyboard app owned by Tencent, began receiving DarkVigil implants. The number and geographic spread of victims initially led ESET to suspect an exploit.

A Sogou component fetched a brand-promotion configuration from a Sogou server over unencrypted HTTP. Domain Name System (DNS) hijacking redirected those requests to attacker-controlled servers, which returned a malicious configuration.

That configuration made the app download the DarkVigil implant and place it where Sogou's own components would run it, giving the malware persistence without a separate mechanism.

ESET does not know where the DNS manipulation occurred. Possibilities include routers set up with malicious DNS settings, routers implanted to hijack DNS and interception at internet service provider (ISP) level.

Des fichiers contenant des données personnelles de certains utilisateurs ont été téléchargés sans autorisation. Parmi les informations compromises figurent des noms, des adresses postales et des détails sur les achats réalisés par les collectionneurs. L’entreprise précise toutefois que les mots de passe, les adresses email réelles et les coordonnées bancaires n’ont pas été exposés.

Delcampe est une entreprise belge fondée en 2000 par Sébastien Delcampe, dont le siège se trouve à Tubize, en Belgique. Spécialisée dans la vente en ligne d’objets de collection, la plateforme permet aux particuliers et aux professionnels d’acheter et de vendre des timbres, des cartes postales, des monnaies, des bandes dessinées et de nombreux autres objets. Présente dans plus de 190 pays, elle revendique plus d’un million d’utilisateurs actifs.

A supplier of the French National Blood Service was hit by a cyber-attack in which hackers turned cold rooms hosting blood samples up to 110°C (230°F)

Read more about the wave of cyber-attacks on refrigeration control systems in Europe:

Cold storage rooms in France's National Blood Service (EFS) were turned to a boiling temperature of 110°C (230°F) in a cyber-attack targeting temperature-controlled storage and refrigeration equipment provider Coolworld.

On November 3, French investigative weekly newspaper Le Canard enchaîné reported a new wave of attacks targeting refrigeration systems in France.

The outlet said unauthorized actors took control of some refrigeration controllers in EFS’s cold storage rooms in the night between November 1 and 2, notably in facilities in the Burgundy and Franche-Comté region, in east-central France.

These cold storage units host blood samples used for health monitoring but also plasma intended for transfusions. While they are typically kept at -30°C (-22°F), the newspaper reported some rooms hit up to 110°C (230°F). This does not mean the equipment or any blood samples reached these temperatures.

The refrigeration control systems of the affected EFS cold rooms are maintained by Coolworld, a Dutch temperature control rental company operating in France, Germany, Ireland, the Netherlands and the UK.

Attendu à l’ordre du jour de la session parlementaire extraordinaire de juillet dernier, le Projet de loi relatif à « la résilience des infrastructures critiques et au renforcement de la cybersécurité » qui porte la transposition de NIS 2 , avait finalement été reporté au 7 octobre…avant d’être retirer de l’ordre du jour « en raison de l’encombrement du calendrier parlementaire ». Tandis que la France expérimente une vague de cyberattaques, visant les services publics autant que le secteur privé, la transposition de la directive NIS 2 par les parlementaires français vient de dépasser de deux années le délai fixé par Bruxelles au 17 octobre 2024. Son titre Ier modernise le dispositif français de sécurité des activités d’importance vitale (SAIV), créé en 2006 et applicable à plus de 300 opérateurs. Signal de veille — The Record.

Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, is facing up to 20 years in prison on wire fraud and money laundering charges after admitting to using his position on an FBI investigative squad to steal more than $2.4 million in cryptocurrency to cover his debts.

A senior FBI official pleaded guilty to stealing millions in cryptocurrency from wallets controlled by nation-state hackers and theft victims.

Yaroch was an FBI Supervisory Special Agent who worked at FBI Headquarters within the Counterintelligence and Espionage Division — with his work focusing on an unnamed nation-state.

He used his seniority to access FBI systems that had the codes and passwords necessary to take cryptocurrency from at least two adversarial nations as well as 10 victims of crimes. In total, he conducted 100 transfers from 79 wallets starting in December 2024. The wallets were connected to 35 different FBI investigations.

Yaroch had hundreds of thousands of dollars in credit card debt, loans and car payments. He paid off several large loans. The Justice Department gained access to his ChatGPT conversations, which showed he planned to buy a vineyard in Portugal and retire.

Yaroch began to make legal arrangements in Portugal and bought plane tickets to the country for him, his wife and his child slated for September. But he ended up confessing to the theft to a DOJ employee in July.

Yaroch told the DOJ employee, who he knew from a previous job, that he was angry about an investigation of a suspect from an unnamed adversarial nation. Yaroch "became frustrated when he could not do more to disrupt this individual's use of cryptocurrency.”

The U.S. is working on extraditing three suspects from Europe in a case involving more than $100 million in fraud from CEO impersonations.

Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan and Guy Sheetrit are accused of pretending to be company CEOs or lawyers and contacting lower-level employees to trick them into sending large payments to bank accounts they controlled.

Soall and Hazan were arrested in Spain this summer and Sheetrit was detained in the U.K. in September. The Justice Department said on Thursday that extradition requests for all three men are pending.

Hazan, 54, and Sheetrit, 42, are from Israel while Soall, 41, is Spanish. All three are facing up to 104 years in prison on multiple charges of money laundering, aggravated identity theft, wire fraud and more.

According to prosecutors, the conspiracy ran from 2024 to 2026 and involved the three as well as other co-conspirators deploying artificial intelligence as a way to spoof the voices and images of real corporate executives.

Court documents said several incidents involved the three men contacting employees and telling them they needed help with a confidential financial transaction, mimicking the CEO’s voice or image on the call.

To further the scheme, they would tell the employee to speak with lawyers at a large international firm that were working on the transaction — using AI to then make themselves look and sound like those lawyers.

Signal de veille — Schneier on Sec..

This is fascinating : The video describes a technique that can reveal where an otherwise unidentifiable recording was made by analyzing its audio for the faint sounds of passing aircraft. The technique is both fascinating and frightening. It works by looking at Doppler curves, which plot the way a plane’s sound changes as it passes overhead because of the Doppler effect. This is the same familiar Doppler effect that causes the frequency of a siren to rise as it approaches and then fall as it passes by and moves away. More generally, it’s the phenomenon whereby the frequency of a wave perceived by an observer changes when the observer and the source of the wave are moving in relation to one another. […] It’s sound that’s relevant here, though, and specifically the sound of aeroplanes. Early in his video, Colsto brings up a map of the flights that were in the air at the time the video he’s tracing was recorded. Much of this information is publicly available. Aircraft equipped with Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast (ADS-B) transmit data about their position, velocity, and altitude, which flight-tracking services collect and make available to the public. While not every plane is tracked, the system provides an enormous amount of information about aircraft movements.

Overall, Chinese-aligned detection trends broadly coincided with changes in Chinese military and maritime activity around Taiwan. For example, cyber activity rose slightly from June to July 2026 at the same time as China expanded coast guard-led ‘gray-zone’ operations around the Island.

This activity includes reports of Chinese coast guard ships patrolling Taiwan-controlled waters.

Despite the sharp fall in China-aligned detections, observed PRC cyber activity remained “substantially higher” than nation-state cyber activity from Russia and Iran during the period, the researchers noted.
